Every confirmation, warning, and error message shown as a transient notification shall be translated (FR-DA-I18N-07), announced to assistive technologies through a polite live region, and remain readable long enough to act on.
Wide matrices and tables shall scroll inside their own container, keeping the first column visible, so the page never scrolls horizontally on a 390-pixel viewport.
SME users shall complete onboarding within 1 day and need less than 4 hours of training, helped by guided workflows (configurable targets).
User satisfaction shall be measured, with a configurable target (default NPS of 30 or more).
Every layout — navigation, tables, and charts — shall render correctly mirrored under Arabic RTL, not just with mirrored text direction.
The system shall support configurable languages (default English, French, Arabic, Spanish, German), currencies (default USD, EUR, MAD, ZAR) and regional date, time and number formats.

Installation shall succeed on a fresh target machine with only a supported Node.js runtime installed — no native C/C++ build toolchain, no required external database server, and no mandatory external API key.
The same source shall run unmodified across supported operating systems via standard package-manager install/build/start commands.

Every change shall be built by a continuous-integration pipeline on Linux, Windows, and macOS that installs dependencies, seeds the demonstration data, runs the automated tests — including the cross-tenant suite of NFR-DA-SEC-11 — and builds the web client.
A CI workflow for Linux, Windows and macOS is provided in .github/workflows; it runs when the repository is hosted on GitHub.
Each tier shall install, seed, and start with its package manager's standard commands (install, seed, dev or start), documented in a README at the root of the delivery.

Cross-cutting engines — the Action/Task Register, the Alert & Notification Engine, the RBAC layer, the KPI/Reporting engine, and the Audit Trail Service — shall be implemented as composable modules reusable by sibling Dynamic Apps via the same API contract.
Single-source modules for entitlements, alerts, AI
AI agent implementations shall be isolated behind a stable internal interface so a rule-based implementation can be replaced by an LLM/vector-DB-backed one without changing calling code.
The Solution Pack feature and quota matrix shall be defined in exactly one place and consumed by every enforcing route, so entitlements can never drift between routes.

The AI Use Case Library's generation service shall be the single designated server-side integration point for a live LLM call and its provider-specific credential/endpoint logic; no other module shall embed its own LLM provider client.
The alert type-to-name and type-to-stage/process mapping shall be defined in exactly one shared module, consumed by both seed data and live computation.

The Installation Guide and User Guide shall be generated from source in Word and PDF, each with an automatic table of contents, and the User Guide's step-by-step walkthroughs shall be replayed automatically against a freshly seeded instance, so the documentation cannot drift from the application.
Guides are generated from source in Word and PDF with an automatic TOC; walkthrough replay is scripted in tools, run at release.

Every User Guide walkthrough shall start from the tenancy — create or choose the Group (Yes/No), create the Organization, then the principal record(s) — and the guide shall include the decision matrix of FR-DA-HLP-04.

Verticals, SME tracks, complexity criteria, packs, project templates, gates and checklists shall be configuration data loaded without code changes, and the platform shall be modular with zero-downtime upgrades, monitoring, alerting and comprehensive logging.
The application shall target evergreen desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers; no legacy-browser support is in scope.
Evergreen browsers; BPMN XML round trip

BPMN diagrams shall be stored and exchanged as schema-valid BPMN 2.0 XML, verified by a round-trip import/export, so a diagram authored in one Dynamic App opens without error in any other BPMN 2.0-compliant tool, and vice versa.

The application's core workflows (record CRUD, approvals, alerts) shall remain fully usable on a mobile viewport without requiring a separate native application; a native or installable Progressive Web App wrapper, where offered, shall consume the same REST API (Section 7.2) with no mobile-specific endpoint variant.
Every AI-generated suggestion shall be logged with a confidence indicator and be attributable to a specific agent/use case and record, or, for the AI Assistant, to the requesting user and question.
COSO coverage, AI log confidence, non-certification disclosure
The Controls module shall support demonstrating COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework coverage across all five components.
The system shall retain the full version history of every AI Use Case and every template indefinitely (no hard deletion of prior versions on edit or revert).

The system shall let verticals map to sector standards — for example IATF 16949 (automotive), AS9100 (aerospace), EU MDR and ISO 13485 (medical devices), FDA 21 CFR Part 11 (pharmaceutical), HACCP (food safety) — as scaffolds subject to FR-DA-CFG-09; certification (ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, GDPR) is an attribute of a deployment, not of the software.

Every requirement of a Dynamic App shall be traceable to its business requirement, user story, test case, release and, where applicable, customer commitment, in line with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148; requirement changes shall be classified Minor, Moderate, Major or Breaking with the matching approval and regression scope.

By default, and whenever no Real LLM Provider Connection is configured, the system shall not transmit tenant data to any third-party service; every AI capability shall run entirely within the deployment's own infrastructure using rule-based/statistical methods and RAG grounding. Only an explicitly user-configured, client-stored Real LLM Provider Connection may cause a single generation request to be sent to that user-selected third-party provider — opt-in per user, never enabled by default, and never applied to a permission-scoped data-query mode.
No external call unless a user adds a model key
The system shall support both shared-infrastructure (SaaS) and dedicated/sovereign deployment options per Organization, without changing the tenant-isolation guarantee.
